node.name: tsym
node.description: transparent alias for the external `tsym` CLI
node.whenToUse: a question is about how TypeScript code is structured or connected — the shape of a directory or file, where a symbol is declared, its resolved type, who calls it, what it calls, what renders or implements it, what breaks if it changes — rather than about text.

passthrough.installHint: Install the tsym CLI: npm install -g @crouton-kit/tsym

rootEntry.concept: what the TypeScript compiler knows about a codebase, exposed for progressive disclosure
rootEntry.description: forwards verbatim to the external `tsym` binary
rootEntry.whenToUse: Use this before reading or grepping TypeScript to understand how code is structured or connected: `outline` a directory or file instead of opening it, `inspect` a symbol for who calls it, what it calls, what renders or implements it, `show`/`type` for one declaration without its file. Answers come from the type checker, so act on them without re-reading to confirm. Grep only for text the compiler cannot see — log strings, comments, config keys, SQL.

node.summary: transparent alias for the external `tsym` CLI — every argument forwards verbatim
node.model: This branch owns no schema of its own: it execs `tsym` with whatever args follow, inherits stdio, and propagates its exit code. Run `crtr tsym -h` for the real command tree.
